hero.venue: ICASSP 2026 · Oral · Information Forensics and Security
hero.paper_title: Membership Inference Attack Against Music Diffusion Models via Generative Manifold Perturbation
hero.deck: We replace a noisy endpoint signal with a behavioral stability score: the minimum time-normalized latent perturbation required to cross a fixed perceptual degradation threshold.
hero.ledger_note: Aggregate results, not a claim about every sample.
audit.title: What are we auditing?
audit.intro: Given a candidate audio clip and an audited music diffusion model, estimate whether the clip was used during training.
audit.flow_question: Was this clip used during training?
audit.member_body: The clip belongs to the target model’s training set.
audit.nonmember_body: The clip was not included in the target model’s training set.
audit.boundary: Membership inference produces a statistical audit signal. It is not training-data extraction, model inversion, attribute inference, or standalone legal proof of copyright infringement.
primer.title: Diffusion models in 60 seconds
primer.intro: Before discussing membership, we need one piece of background: a diffusion model learns to reverse a gradual noising process.
primer.stage_forward_note: Add Gaussian noise according to timestep t
primer.forward_body: The forward process mixes clean audio with Gaussian noise according to timestep t. A trained diffusion model learns a reverse mapping that progressively removes this noise.
primer.reverse_body: LSA-Probe does not only inspect the final reconstruction error. It intervenes at an intermediate state and observes how stable the learned reverse mapping is around that candidate.
primer.boundary: The paper finds the strongest membership separation around the middle of the reverse trajectory, with t_ratio=0.6 used in the main setting. This is an experimental finding in the evaluated settings, not a universal property of every diffusion model.
primer.focus_bridge: Probe an intermediate state and measure how much intervention is required to destabilize its learned reverse mapping.
innovation.title: What does LSA-Probe change?
innovation.card1_body: Replace a noisy single reconstruction signal with the minimum intervention required to destabilize the local reverse process.
innovation.card2_body: Scale the perturbation by the natural forward-noise level so that budgets are comparable across diffusion timesteps.
innovation.card3_body: Use inner PGD to search for a degradation direction and outer bisection to find the smallest successful budget.
innovation.note: The resulting score does not require an explicit likelihood or a separately trained shadow model.
threat.title: A strong, explicit white-box threat model
threat.intro: LSA-Probe is designed for a developer or authorized auditor who can inspect and differentiate through the model’s reverse process.
threat.point1: Can run forward diffusion and deterministic reverse sampling.
threat.point2: Can compute gradients with respect to an intermediate diffusion state.
threat.point3: Does not need shadow models or member labels from the target model.
threat.point4: Does need an independent non-member development set for calibration.
threat.boundary: LSA-Probe is best understood as an authorized internal audit method, not a remote black-box attack available to an ordinary user.
endpoint.title: Why endpoint reconstruction error is insufficient
endpoint.intro: A single reconstruction loss is a noisy endpoint observation, especially in the strict low-FPR regime that matters for high-cost audits.
endpoint.factor1_body: Reconstruction error changes with the diffusion state.
endpoint.factor2_body: Injected noise and sampling choices alter the endpoint.
endpoint.factor3_body: Timbre and musical complexity can confound raw loss.
endpoint.factor4_body: Waveform MSE need not track what listeners perceive.
endpoint.conclusion: Instead of asking whether one reconstruction has a small error, LSA-Probe asks how much worst-case, time-normalized intervention is required to destabilize the local reverse process.
insight.title: Measure the intervention required to break local stability
insight.body: Training members empirically occupy more stable local regions of the learned reverse mapping. They require a larger bounded perturbation to reach the same perceptual degradation target.
insight.caption: Conceptual schematic — not measured sample data
insight.score_body: Minimum perturbation budget that reaches the fixed perceptual degradation target.
insight.caution: This is an empirical local-geometric interpretation, not an analytic recovery of a data manifold or a universal claim about diffusion models.
intuition.title: First-order intuition: why should members require a larger budget?
intuition.body: The local Jacobian describes how sensitive the reverse mapping is to a small intervention around the candidate state. If the learned mapping is locally smoother around a training member, the same perturbation budget produces less output degradation. Reaching the fixed threshold τ therefore requires a larger budget, producing a larger Cadv.
intuition.relation: Lower local sensitivity → larger required budget → higher Cadv → more member-like
intuition.boundary: This is a local, first-order interpretation of the empirical stability signal. It is not an analytic recovery of the data manifold and not a universal theorem that applies to every diffusion model.
threshold.title: Two thresholds, two different jobs
threshold.tau_body: Defines the degradation target. It is calibrated as P95 on an independent non-member development set at ηref=0.05. It is not the membership cutoff.
threshold.score_body: Measures the minimum time-normalized budget required to reach τ for each candidate.
threshold.decision_body: A separate cutoff on Cadv defines the operating point, such as FPR=1%, and yields TPR@1% FPR.
method.title: Inner PGD finds direction; outer bisection finds cost
method.intro: The method searches for a strong local degradation direction at each budget, then finds the smallest successful budget.
method.framework_caption: Author-provided expanded framework, checked against Figure 1 in the paper. Image pixels are unchanged.
method.step1: Forward diffuse the candidate to an intermediate state.
method.step3: Use inner PGD to find the strongest degradation direction.
method.step4: Use outer bisection to find the minimum successful budget.
method.normalisation: The raw scale of an intervention is not comparable across diffusion timesteps because the forward noise variance changes with t. Scaling δ̃ by σt places the perturbation on the timestep’s natural noise scale.
model_paths.title: One probe, two diffusion families
model_paths.wave2: Forward-noise it to waveform state xₜ.
model_paths.wave3: Apply δₜ=σₜδ̃ directly in waveform space.
model_paths.latent1: Encode the waveform with the VAE encoder: z₀=Enc(x₀).
model_paths.latent2: Forward-noise it to latent state zₜ.
model_paths.latent3: Apply the time-normalized perturbation in latent space.
model_paths.latent6: Measure perceptual distance on the resulting waveforms.
model_paths.control1: The forward noise is fixed for each paired evaluation so that the measured difference reflects the added intervention rather than a new random noise realization.
model_paths.control2: When conditioning is used, the text prompt and guidance remain fixed between the clean and perturbed reverse passes.
walkthrough.kicker: Algorithm walkthrough · Illustrative control flow · Not a measured sample
walkthrough.title: Watch the two loops coordinate
walkthrough.ready: Ready. Start with the full admissible interval.
walkthrough.state2: Run the inner PGD search within the current budget.
walkthrough.state3: Compare the strongest perceptual degradation with τ.
walkthrough.state4: Update one side of the bisection interval.
walkthrough.state5: Repeat until the interval is tight; report Cadv≈u.
evidence.title: Evidence at the strict low-FPR operating point
evidence.intro: All values below are transcribed from Table 1. No per-sample distributions or ROC points are reconstructed.
evidence.missed: Members still missed at the best strict operating point
evidence.interpret_title: What the result does—and does not—show
evidence.interpret: LSA-Probe consistently improves the strict low-FPR operating point, but the best TPR at 1% FPR is 20%. The method therefore provides a stronger audit signal without solving membership auditing outright. Precision still depends on the real member base rate.
low_fpr.title: Why focus on TPR at only 1% FPR?
low_fpr.body: Membership auditing is a high-cost decision problem. When the non-member population is much larger than the member population, even a seemingly small false-positive rate can produce many false alerts. The operating point must therefore control false positives before recall is interpreted.
low_fpr.example: Among 10,000 non-members, an FPR of 1% corresponds to approximately 100 false positives.
low_fpr.point3: Precision depends on the true member base rate.
low_fpr.point4: A membership score is not standalone legal evidence.
baselines.title: What is LSA-Probe compared against?
baselines.endpoint_signal: Denoising or reconstruction loss measured at a timestep or at the endpoint.
baselines.endpoint_diff: A single loss can be confounded by timestep, noise seed, content complexity and perceptual mismatch.
baselines.trajectory_signal: Distance between a recovered diffusion-trajectory point and the model-predicted trajectory point.
baselines.trajectory_diff: Measures trajectory mismatch rather than the minimum worst-case intervention required to cross a perceptual threshold.
baselines.secmi_signal: A diffusion-process membership signal used as an existing comparison baseline.
baselines.secmi_diff: Does not use LSA-Probe’s time-normalized adversarial-cost construction.
baselines.lsa_signal: The minimum time-normalized perturbation budget required to exceed a fixed perceptual degradation threshold.
baselines.lsa_diff: Measures local generative stability using inner PGD and outer bisection.
baselines.compute: All baselines were matched within ±5% per-sample wall-clock time on an A100-80GB.

reliability.title: How the evidence was controlled
reliability.intro: The evaluation spans waveform and latent diffusion, two music domains, leakage controls, uncertainty estimates and compute-matched baselines.
reliability.setup: Deterministic DDIM · t_ratio=0.6 · p=2 · ηmax=0.8 · CDPAM · 22.05 kHz training audio · in-graph resampling to 16 kHz for metrics.
reliability.split: Piece/artist splits for MAESTRO; track/artist splits for FMA; Chromaprint + LSH duplicate and cover checks with manual review.
reliability.stats: DeLong AUC intervals; sample-level bootstrap elsewhere; 10,000 resamples; Holm–Bonferroni correction.
reliability.compute: B=10 outer × K=12 inner, roughly (K+2)B reverse passes per sample; baselines matched within ±5% wall-clock on an A100-80GB.
limitations.title: Limitations and open questions
limitations.item1: Strong white-box access is required: parameters, sampler, intermediate states and gradients.
limitations.item2: Repeated PGD, restarts and bisection make the audit computationally expensive.
limitations.item3: The best TPR@1% FPR is still only 20%.
limitations.item4: Evaluation covers two model families and two music datasets.
limitations.item5: Threshold calibration depends on an independent non-member development set.
limitations.item6: Cross-model and cross-domain threshold transfer remain underexplored.
limitations.item7: Results do not directly generalize to text LLMs or multimodal agents.
limitations.item8: A membership score is not standalone legal evidence.
limitations.item9: “Generative manifold” is an empirical local-geometric description, not an analytically recovered manifold.
limitations.item10: Defenses need further study: differential privacy, regularization, deduplication, audit-aware training and reduced memorization.
defense.title: Defensive implications and open evaluation questions
defense.status: Not experimentally evaluated in the current paper
defense.card1_body: Deduplication, artist-aware splitting and provenance control reduce accidental duplication and leakage, but do not by themselves guarantee the absence of memorization.
defense.card2_body: Regularization, early stopping, audit-aware training and differential privacy are potential directions for reducing membership leakage.
defense.card3_body: LSA-Probe requires parameters, intermediate states and gradients. Restricting access changes the practical threat surface, although it does not eliminate the underlying memorization risk.
defense.card4_body: A meaningful defense evaluation must consider an auditor or attacker who knows the defense and can recalibrate the probe, threshold or optimization procedure.
agent.title: From Generative-Model Auditing to Agent Safety
agent.subtitle: A methodological transfer, not an experimental result of LSA-Probe.
agent.agent1: Define protected user data, memory, retrieved content and tool permissions
agent.agent2: Build authorized internal red-team and audit infrastructure
agent.lsa3: Measure the minimum intervention needed to destabilize a trajectory
agent.agent3: Measure the minimum bounded intervention needed to change a decision or tool action
agent.lsa4: Evaluate at strict low-FPR operating points
agent.agent4: Control false alarms before blocking legitimate tasks or users
agent.agent5: Preserve audit trails and uncertainty rather than issuing absolute claims
agent.transfers: Asset definition, authorized access, bounded intervention, strict operating points and uncertainty-aware audit trails.
agent.not_body: Audio latents are not LLM hidden states; diffusion trajectories are not agent plans. LSA-Probe does not detect prompt injection, stop jailbreaks, solve tool authorization, provide trusted execution or establish effectiveness for mobile agents.
agent.direction: Generalize stability-based auditing from generative trajectories to agent decision trajectories: measure the minimum bounded intervention required to trigger an unsafe decision while jointly tracking task utility and side effects.
resources.title: Verify the primary sources
resources.intro: The public repository currently exposes a project README rather than a complete implementation or checkpoints.
focus.audit_boundary: For developers or authorized auditors—not a remote black-box attack available to an ordinary user.
focus.tau_short: Perceptual degradation target; not the membership cutoff
focus.cutoff_short: A separate threshold sets the FPR operating point
focus.normalization_body: Natural noise scale changes with diffusion time, so raw perturbation norms are not directly comparable. Time normalization makes budgets comparable across timesteps.
focus.evidence_point1: The strict low-FPR operating point improves in all four model–dataset combinations.
focus.evidence_point2: Best TPR@1% FPR is still 20%, so roughly 80% of members remain missed in the best case.
focus.evidence_point3: The method strengthens the audit signal; it does not solve membership auditing outright.
focus.evidence_point4: Precision still depends on the true member base rate.
focus.reliability_title: How the evidence was controlled—and where it stops
focus.data_controls_body: MAESTRO piece/artist split · FMA track/artist split · Chromaprint + LSH + manual review.
focus.stats_body: DeLong for AUC · 10,000 bootstrap resamples elsewhere · Holm–Bonferroni correction.
focus.compute_body: B=10 outer · K=12 inner · roughly (K+2)B reverse passes · baselines matched within ±5% wall-clock on A100-80GB.
focus.defense_short: Potential directions include data hygiene, memorization reduction, access control and adaptive evaluation against defenses.
focus.asset_agent: User data, memory, retrieved content and tool permissions
focus.intervention_agent: Change an agent decision or tool action
focus.operating_agent: Avoid blocking legitimate users or safe tasks because of false alarms
focus.transfers_short: Asset definition · authorized internal auditing · bounded worst-case intervention · strict low-FPR evaluation · uncertainty-aware audit trails.
focus.not_short: Audio latents are not LLM hidden states; diffusion trajectories are not agent plans. The paper does not establish protection against prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe tool calls or mobile-agent attacks.
focus.future_label: Possible research direction — not a result of this paper
focus.future_body: Generalize stability-based auditing to agent decision trajectories while jointly measuring unsafe decisions, task utility and side effects.
